draft.title: Linear functions
card: The gradient m of a line is rise ÷ run. For points (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂), m = (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁).
m is the gradient and c is the y-intercept, where the line crosses the y-axis.
use this when you know the gradient m and one point (x₁, y₁) on the line. Example: m = 2 through (3, 1) gives y − 1 = 2(x − 3), so y = 2x − 5.
Parallel lines have equal gradients. Perpendicular lines have gradients that multiply to −1, so a line with gradient 2 is perpendicular to a line with gradient −1/2.
draft.remember: Gradient is rise over run. Parallel: same m. Perpendicular: m₁ × m₂ = −1.

a.q: What is the gradient of the line through (1, 2) and (4, 11)?
a.why: m = (11 − 2) ÷ (4 − 1) = 9 ÷ 3 = 3. The option 1/3 comes from putting run over rise, which is the wrong way round.
a.clue: Rise goes on top, run goes on the bottom.

b.q: A line has gradient 2/3 and passes through (6, 1). Which line through the same point is perpendicular to it?
b.why: The perpendicular gradient m satisfies 2/3 × m = −1, so m = −3/2. Using the point (6, 1) gives y − 1 = −3/2(x − 6). The option with 3/2 only flips the fraction and does not change the sign, so the product is 1, not −1.
b.clue: Flip the fraction and change the sign.

check.summary: No problems found. The card's worked example (y = 2x − 5) and both answers (gradient 3, and y − 1 = −3/2(x − 6)) check out, and the explanations match the card.

final.title: Linear functions
card: The gradient \(m\) of a line is \(\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}}\). For points \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) and \((x_{2}, y_{2})\), \(m = \frac{y_{2} - y_{1}}{x_{2} - x_{1}}\).
\(m\) is the gradient and \(c\) is the y-intercept, where the line crosses the y-axis.
use this when you know the gradient \(m\) and one point \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) on the line. Example: \(m = 2\) through \((3, 1)\) gives \(y - 1 = 2(x - 3)\), so \(y = 2x - 5\).
Parallel lines have equal gradients. Perpendicular lines have gradients that multiply to \(-1\), so a line with gradient 2 is perpendicular to a line with gradient \(-\frac{1}{2}\).

3.alt: The line \(y = 2x - 5\). It passes through \((3, 1)\) and crosses the y-axis at \((0, -5)\). From \((3, 1)\), a run of 1 to the right and a rise of 2 up reach \((4, 3)\), so the gradient is 2.

final.remember: Gradient is rise over run. Parallel: same \(m\). Perpendicular: \(m_{1} \times m_{2} = -1\).

a.q: What is the gradient of the line through \((1, 2)\) and \((4, 11)\)?
a.why: \(m = \frac{11 - 2}{4 - 1} = \frac{9}{3} = 3\). The option \(\frac{1}{3}\) comes from putting run over rise, which is the wrong way round.
a.clue: Rise goes on top, run goes on the bottom.

b.q: A line has gradient \(\frac{2}{3}\) and passes through \((6, 1)\). Which line through the same point is perpendicular to it?
b.why: The perpendicular gradient \(m\) satisfies \(\frac{2}{3} \times m = -1\), so \(m = -\frac{3}{2}\). Using the point \((6, 1)\) gives \(y - 1 = -\frac{3}{2}(x - 6)\). The option with \(\frac{3}{2}\) only flips the fraction and does not change the sign, so the product is 1, not \(-1\).
b.clue: Flip the fraction and change the sign.
